# text.library: ParseNumber

**Status:** Supported (tier `foundation`). In a shipping tier; the lint, type-check, and code-generation gates cover it. No release promises its signature yet.

## Summary

> Reads a real number in the P21 forms: optional sign, digits, optional point and
> digits, optional exponent E or e with an optional sign. "1.", ".5" and "1.E-06"
> are accepted; anything else, and a value that rounds to infinity, has Ok false
> and Value 0. The value is correctly rounded, so every runtime agrees bit for bit.
> Witness: ParseNumber("1.5E1") is (15, true); ParseNumber("1e") is (0, false).

## Signature

```plato
ParseNumber(s: String): NumberParse
```

### Law_ParseNumberAcceptedForms

```plato
// Two-line witness: the accepted forms and their values.
Law_ParseNumberAcceptedForms(): Boolean
    => ParseNumber("1.5E1").Ok && ParseNumber("1.5E1").Value == 15.0 && ParseNumber("1.").Value == 1.0
    && ParseNumber(".5").Value == 0.5 && ParseNumber("1.E-06").Value == 0.000001 && ParseNumber("-2.5e+1").Value == -25.0
    && ParseNumber("+7").Value == 7.0 && ParseNumber("0").Ok && ParseNumber("1.").Ok && ParseNumber(".5").Ok && ParseNumber("1.E-06").Ok;
```

// Two-line witness: the rejected forms are Ok false with Value 0.
Law_ParseNumberRejectedForms(): Boolean
    => !ParseNumber("").Ok && !ParseNumber(".").Ok && !ParseNumber("-").Ok && !ParseNumber("1e").Ok && !ParseNumber("1e+").Ok
    && !ParseNumber("NaN").Ok && !ParseNumber("Infinity").Ok && !ParseNumber("0x10").Ok && !ParseNumber(" 1").Ok
    && !ParseNumber("1 ").Ok && !ParseNumber("1,5").Ok && !ParseNumber("1.5.2").Ok && !ParseNumber("1e999").Ok
    && ParseNumber("1e999").Value == 0.0 && ParseNumber("abc").Value == 0.0;

### Law_ParseNumberRejectsLetters

[stdlib/tests/text.laws.plato, line 89](../../../../../stdlib/tests/text.laws.plato#L89)

```plato
// A text of letters, the runner's String, is never a number.
Law_ParseNumberRejectsLetters(s: String): Boolean
    => s.Count == 0 || !ParseNumber(s).Ok;
```

### Law_ParseNumberIsCorrectlyRounded

[stdlib/tests/text.laws.plato, line 94](../../../../../stdlib/tests/text.laws.plato#L94)

```plato
// Correct rounding: a decimal exactly halfway between two Numbers rounds to even, and the
// nearest Number to 0.1 is the one the literal 0.1 denotes.
Law_ParseNumberIsCorrectlyRounded(): Boolean
    => ParseNumber("0.1").Value == 0.1 && ParseNumber("9007199254740993").Value == 9007199254740992.0
    && ParseNumber("9007199254740995").Value == 9007199254740996.0 && ParseNumber("1e-400").Value == 0.0
    && ParseNumber("4.9e-324").Value > 0.0;
```

### Law_ParseNumberKeepsNegativeZero

[stdlib/tests/text.laws.plato, line 100](../../../../../stdlib/tests/text.laws.plato#L100)

```plato
// Negative zero survives: 1 / ParseNumber("-0") is negative infinity.
Law_ParseNumberKeepsNegativeZero(): Boolean
    => 1.0 / ParseNumber("-0").Value < 0.0 && 1.0 / ParseNumber("0").Value > 0.0;
```

### Law_ParseNumberRoundTripsNumberToShortestString

[stdlib/tests/text.laws.plato, line 130](../../../../../stdlib/tests/text.laws.plato#L130)

```plato
// The round trip: reading the shortest text of a finite Number gives back that Number
// exactly, sign of zero included (1 / x tells 0 from -0). The runner draws Numbers from
// [-10, 10] and a few special values.
Law_ParseNumberRoundTripsNumberToShortestString(x: Number): Boolean
    => ParseNumber(NumberToShortestString(x)).Ok
    && ParseNumber(NumberToShortestString(x)).Value == x
    && 1.0 / ParseNumber(NumberToShortestString(x)).Value == 1.0 / x;
```

### Law_NonFiniteNumbersHaveTextThatIsNotANumber

[stdlib/tests/text.laws.plato, line 150](../../../../../stdlib/tests/text.laws.plato#L150)

```plato
Law_NonFiniteNumbersHaveTextThatIsNotANumber(): Boolean
    => NumberToShortestString(0.0 / 0.0) == "NaN" && NumberToShortestString(1.0 / 0.0) == "Infinity"
    && NumberToShortestString(-1.0 / 0.0) == "-Infinity"
    && !ParseNumber("NaN").Ok && !ParseNumber("Infinity").Ok && !ParseNumber("-Infinity").Ok;
```

### Line 1

**Source:** [stdlib/foundation/text.library.plato, line 1](../../../../../stdlib/foundation/text.library.plato#L1).

```plato
//==
// # Text
//
// Reading numbers from text. The host half is in `intrinsics.library.plato`
// (`IsNumberText`, `NumberFromText`, `IsIntegerText`, `IntegerFromText`); the functions
// here return it as a record the caller checks.

library Text
{
    // Reads a real number in the P21 forms: optional sign, digits, optional point and
    // digits, optional exponent E or e with an optional sign. "1.", ".5" and "1.E-06"
    // are accepted; anything else, and a value that rounds to infinity, has Ok false
    // and Value 0. The value is correctly rounded, so every runtime agrees bit for bit.
    // Witness: ParseNumber("1.5E1") is (15, true); ParseNumber("1e") is (0, false).
    ParseNumber(s: String): NumberParse
        => NumberParse(s.NumberFromText, s.IsNumberText);
```
